title: Black Holes and Event Horizons
text: A black hole is a region of spacetime where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light or other electromagnetic radiation, has enough energy to escape. The boundary of the region from which no escape is possible is called the event horizon. Black holes are formed when massive stars collapse under their own gravity at the end of their lives in a supernova explosion. Supermassive black holes, with masses millions to billions of times that of the Sun, are found at the centers of most large galaxies, including the Milky Way. Stephen Hawking theorized that black holes can slowly lose mass through quantum effects, now known as Hawking radiation.
